pages.text: "What is that? It looks nothing like it!" Gugu, the broad-chested pigeon, said bluntly. Kiki, the pointy-eared cat, was drawing on the foggy window by the stove.
Kiki wiped away the drawing with a sleeve. Nono, the smallest, roundest sparrow, buried his beak in his scarf. Gugu had wanted all three to draw together.
Kiki and Nono moved to the far end of the bench. No one sat beside Gugu. "Oh? My next seat is empty."
Fresh bread smelled lovely. Grandpa held a loaf in both hands and offered it to Gugu. "Hot, right? Take it with both hands."
Gugu took it. Warm palms, rising steam. Holding the bread, Gugu remembered those earlier words.
"My words were not warm at all." Gugu tried shaping different words. Instead of "It looks nothing like it"... "Words as warm as bread!"
Gugu went to Kiki. "Sorry about before. What is your drawing? I want to try too." Kiki's ears pricked forward. Nono came over.
Grandpa dried his hands with a cloth. "How was the bread you took in both hands, Gugu?" "Warm!" Gugu answered.
They drew side by side on the misty window. "One, think first! Two, make your words warm! Three, say thank you first!" Nono drew a circle. "Wow, nice drawing!" Gugu said.
Kiki rested a head on Gugu's shoulder. Warm words come back warmly. Gugu flicked the green bag strap. "Words as warm as bread!"
